result.title: Benchmark Prediction with Sparse and Unpaired Cached Responses
result.summary: Evaluating a generative model on all queries from all available benchmark tasks is prohibitively expensive. As such, models are often evaluated on different subsets of tasks and/or different subsets of queries from a given task. The resulting collection of responses and the corresponding (model, task) score matrix are sparse and unpaired. In this paper, we introduce the Product Kernel Perspective Space (PKPS), a collection of low-dimensional representations of models based on their embedded responses. PKPS generalizes existing methods for representing black-box generative models by comparing responses to similar -- rather than just identical -- queries and is therefore able to utilize sparse and unpaired information. Theoretically, we show that benchmark prediction using PKPS is query-efficient relative to methods that only use information from dense and paired portions of the evaluation data. Empirically, we show that PKPS-based methods outperform baselines on benchmark prediction across two large benchmark suites.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Product Kernel Perspective Space（PKPS），把生成模型响应嵌入到低维表示空间，通过比较相似而不完全相同的查询来利用稀疏、非配对评测数据，并给出查询效率的理论与两个基准套件上的预测实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「比较相似而非相同查询」的核相似度路线，可供核查是否适用于 latent 相似度中查询内容、位置与深度不完全对齐时的比较，以及用稀疏响应预测模型表现以降低评测成本。
